items.title: Rayo-Athletic match abandoned after fans protest against club owner
items.author: David Latona
items.creator: David Latona
items.summary: The LaLiga match between Rayo Vallecano and Athletic Club was abandoned on Saturday after home fans lobbed paper airplanes and small rubber balls onto the pitch in protest against the Madrid club's owner midway through the first half.
items.body:
The LaLiga match between Rayo Vallecano and Athletic Club was abandoned on Saturday after home fans lobbed paper airplanes and small rubber balls onto the pitch in protest against the Madrid club's owner midway through the first half.
The game was the first of this league season played at the Estadio de Vallecas, which was temporarily [USN:L1N43U0P3 TEXT:"closed"] after an audit found serious safety issues.
Rayo fans blame negligence by club owner Raul Martin Presa, who in turn accused regional authorities of deliberately targeting his club.
The Sports Association of Rayo Vallecano fan group said in a statement after the suspension that their protest was "legitimate and democratic... necessary and peaceful."
It added that it was the "consequence of three decades of putting the safety and health of 15,000 people at risk every fortnight".
La Liga said in a statement on social media it "strongly condemned this type of behaviour, which endangers safety and makes the normal development of the competition impossible".
A new date and time for the match will be announced shortly, LaLiga said. Athletic returned to Bilbao, saying on social media that LaLiga had communicated the game would not take place later on Saturday or on Sunday.
Last season's Conference League finalists Rayo released a statement saying the club would seek to identify and discipline those responsible, adding that the forced postponement was part of a sustained campaign of disruption by the fan group.
The players, officials and supporters present were "victims of an attack on their rights and freedoms, committed by an organised group of intolerant individuals," said the statement.
"UNSUSTAINABLE SITUATION" Rayo captain Oscar Valentin said on social media that "an unsustainable situation had reached its limit" and too little had been done to prevent things getting to this point.
"It is necessary to listen to and understand the discontent of our fans. We need a way of bringing ALL parties closer together, always putting the common good first and, above all, the good of Rayo Vallecano," Valentin added.
After Rayo's first three home games were moved to the stadium of second-tier Leganes, registering some of La Liga's lowest-ever attendance figures, home fans started chanting, jeering and whistling against Presa before kickoff on Saturday.
By the 13th minute - when Rayo ultras usually chant the song "Presa leave already" - hundreds of fans launched paper planes and small rubber balls onto the pitch, prompting the referee to suspend play.
A 15-minute pause ensued, during which the stadium's speaker urged spectators not to throw objects onto the field as staff hastily removed them.
When play resumed a little later, fans in the south stand again hurled objects onto the pitch and the referee abandoned the game.
Anger at Presa's management has [USN:L8N3NH005 TEXT:"reached a peak"] in recent months, following the closure of Vallecas Stadium for Rayo's opening home games of the season.
In a friendly against Cagliari last Saturday, anti-Presa graffiti appeared in the VIP box, which fans surrounded in protest before leaving the stadium.

items.title: Several wounded in Riyadh airport attack, operations suspended, Saudi aviation authority says
items.author: Timour Azhari, Enas Alashray
items.creator: Timour Azhari, Enas Alashray
items.summary: Several people were wounded in an attack on King Khalid International Airport in Saudi Arabia's capital Riyadh on Saturday that forced a suspension of operations, the country's civil aviation authority said.
items.body:
Several people were wounded in an attack on King Khalid International Airport in Saudi Arabia's capital Riyadh on Saturday that forced a suspension of operations, the country's civil aviation authority said.
There was no immediate claim of responsibility for the attack, but it comes amid an escalation of [USN:L1N45V08F TEXT:"missile strikes"] by Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis against Saudi Arabia.
The airport had already been struck in two earlier attacks this week that left four people dead and exposed vulnerabilities in the kingdom's ability to defend itself as it wages war on the Houthis. Saudi Arabia's early warning system did not issue an alert ahead of Saturday's incident.
The Saudi government's media office did not immediately respond to questions from Reuters.
One eyewitness at the airport on Saturday reported seeing an explosion and then multiple people lying injured on the ground inside. More than a dozen ambulances were seen rushing towards the facility.
An injured traveller told Reuters they saw something fly across the sky outside the airport before part of the ceiling near a departure gate collapsed.
US TO "LOOK AT" JOINING SAUDI FIGHT AGAINST HOUTHIS: TRUMP Following the attack, US President Donald Trump, speaking to reporters outside the White House, was asked whether the United States planned to join Saudi strikes on the Houthis.
"We may. We're going to look at it. We just found out about the recent attack, so we'll make a decision. We move very quickly," he said.
The US embassy in Riyadh said it was "aware of attacks" and "strongly recommends all US citizens avoid this airport and surrounding areas."
The UK and Irish embassies in Saudi Arabia said in statements on X that they were also aware of a "serious incident" at the airport. The Canadian embassy said that "ongoing military activity" had impacted operations at the airport.
RIYADH DUE TO HOLD MAJOR SUMMITS Flight-tracking site flightradar24 showed all flights to Riyadh had either been diverted or cancelled, with only a helicopter hovering over the airport at one point.
Kuwait Airways said it had cancelled flights to and from the Saudi capital due to what it described as the closure of Riyadh airport because of the "security situation" there.
Etihad Airways and Qatar Airways earlier cancelled multiple flights between their respective hubs and Riyadh, with some cancellations extending into Monday.
Houthi attacks on Thursday and earlier in the week had already prompted a number of carriers to suspend or cancel services to the Saudi capital, shortly before Riyadh is due to host [USN:L8N45W01K TEXT:"major energy and investment conferences"].
Organisers of those conferences said on Saturday they would go ahead as planned, and they sought to reassure attendees of their security.
The Houthis have said airliners should avoid Saudi airspace, declaring it a zone of military operations after the Saudi-backed Yemeni government launched an offensive against the group earlier this month.

items.title: Ronaldo, provisionalmente suspendido por abandono de la selección portuguesa, según medios
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo ha sido suspendido provisionalmente por la Federación Portuguesa de Fútbol (FPF) tras la apertura de un expediente disciplinario por la marcha del delantero de la concentración de la selección nacional, informaron el sábado medios de comunicación portugueses.
items.body:
Cristiano Ronaldo ha sido suspendido provisionalmente por la Federación Portuguesa de Fútbol (FPF) tras la apertura de un expediente disciplinario por la marcha del delantero de la concentración de la selección nacional, informaron el sábado medios de comunicación portugueses.
El jugador, de 41 años, abandonó la concentración del equipo en Copenhague antes del partido de la Liga de Naciones que Portugal disputó contra Dinamarca la semana pasada, tras una desavenencia con el seleccionador Jorge Jesús.
Ronaldo, que no llegó a salir al campo en el partido contra Noruega, acusó a Jesús de haber incumplido en dos ocasiones su palabra respecto a su papel en el equipo.
Según el periódico portugués A Bola, la FPF confirmó que se había abierto un expediente disciplinario.
"Sin perjuicio de la suspensión preventiva automática a la que estaba sujeto hasta la fecha de inicio del procedimiento, se dictó una suspensión preventiva no automática del jugador y se concedió carácter de urgencia al procedimiento", dijo la FPF, según el medio.
Ronaldo se disculpó el martes por no haber saludado a la afición tras el partido contra Noruega y por haber abandonado a sus compañeros de equipo, y añadió que seguiría estando disponible tras cumplir cualquier sanción derivada del incidente.
Reuters se puso en contacto con la Federación Portuguesa de Fútbol para recabar sus comentarios.

items.title: UN Human Rights office condemns racist abuse targeting Gauff
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: The United Nations Human Rights office has condemned online racist abuse faced by Coco Gauff after a replayed point sparked a backlash against the American tennis player this week.
items.body:
The United Nations Human Rights office has condemned online racist abuse faced by Coco Gauff after a replayed point [USN:L4N45S06O TEXT:"sparked a backlash"] against the American tennis player this week.
Gauff was targeted after stopping play during a crucial point in her win over Sun Xinran at the China Open, raising her hand to complain about a flickering advertising board as Sun was about to hit a winner.
The umpire ordered the point to be replayed after a video review, and Gauff went on to win the match 7-5 6-1, but the American later revealed in a social media post that she had received a huge amount of racist abuse following the match.
"You can dislike me or disagree about what happened without being racist," Gauff, who is Black, said on X in reply to a post containing a racial slur.
The official UN Human Rights office posted a statement on Saturday calling for players, coaches and sports bodies to unite against racial and sexist abuse.
"Racist messages such as those targeting tennis player Coco Gauff online are appalling and illustrate that Black female athletes are specifically targeted for vitriol and racial abuse," it wrote on X.
"There is no place in sport for racial or sexist slurs and abuse. Players, coaches, and sports bodies need to stand up for those facing such attacks and fans need to push back against those who sully sport with racism and sexism."
Reuters has contacted the WTA, the governing body of women's tennis, and tournament organisers in Beijing for comment.
Twice Grand Slam winner Gauff [USN:L1N45T0DY TEXT:"exited the tournament"] on Wednesday with a round-of-16 loss, and said the incident had left her drained.
A study by the WTA and World Tennis showed players were subjected to over 12,000 abusive posts and messages on social media in 2025, up from 8,000 posts the previous year.

items.title: Ronaldo provisionally suspended after national team walkout, media reports say
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo has been provisionally suspended by the Portuguese Football Federation (FPF) after disciplinary proceedings were opened over the forward's departure from the national team camp, Portuguese media reported on Saturday.
items.body:
Cristiano Ronaldo has been provisionally suspended by the Portuguese Football Federation (FPF) after disciplinary proceedings were opened over the forward's departure from the national team camp, Portuguese media reported on Saturday.
The 41-year-old left the squad's base in [USN:L6N45M17Z TEXT:"Copenhagen"] before Portugal's Nations League match against Denmark last week, after a rift with head coach Jorge Jesus.
Ronaldo, an unused substitute against Norway, [USN:L6N45M17Z TEXT:"accused Jesus"] of twice breaking his word regarding his role in the team.
After Portugal's 2-1 win, Jesus denied he had made any agreement with the player but left the door open for his return.
According to Portuguese newspaper A Bola, the FPF confirmed that disciplinary proceedings had been opened against Ronaldo.
"Without prejudice to the automatic preventive suspension to which he was subject until the date of initiation, a non-automatic preventive suspension of the player was determined, and the proceedings were given urgent status," the federation was quoted as saying.
FPF president Pedro Proenca said everyone within the federation wanted Ronaldo to return to the national team once the matter was resolved.
"The Portuguese Football Federation and its president, in this spirit of tranquility, speaking with all parties, who have already publicly demonstrated their desire to have the captain back with us, there is an expressed wish from everyone," he was quoted as saying by A Bola.
"This includes the federation, the FPF president, the national team coach, the captain and the players."
Regarding Ronaldo's disciplinary process, Proenca added: "That will depend solely on the Disciplinary Committee, which is an autonomous body, and it will do its job."
Ronaldo apologised on Tuesday for failing to acknowledge supporters after the Norway game and for leaving his teammates, adding that he would remain available for selection after serving any punishment arising from the incident.

FPF president Pedro Proenca said everyone within the federation wanted Ronaldo to return to the national team once the matter was resolved.
"The Portuguese Football Federation and its president, in this spirit of tranquility, speaking with all parties, who have already publicly demonstrated their desire to have the captain back with us, there is an expressed wish from everyone," he was quoted as saying by A Bola.
"This includes the federation, the FPF president, the national team coach, the captain and the players."
Regarding Ronaldo's disciplinary process, Proenca added: "That will depend solely on the Disciplinary Committee, which is an autonomous body, and it will do its job."
Ronaldo apologised on Tuesday for failing to acknowledge supporters after the Norway game and for leaving his teammates, adding that he would remain available for selection after serving any punishment arising from the incident.

items.title: Guimaraes grabs winner as Arsenal rally to beat Leeds
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Arsenal came back from a goal down to beat Leeds United 2-1 at the Emirates Stadium on Saturday, with Brazilian Bruno Guimaraes coming off the bench to net the winner as the Premier League resumed following a lengthy international break.
items.body:
Arsenal came back from a goal down to beat Leeds United 2-1 at the Emirates Stadium on Saturday, with Brazilian Bruno Guimaraes coming off the bench to net the winner as the Premier League resumed following a lengthy international break.
The competition returned under a cloud, with Manchester City found guilty by an independent commission of more than 100 breaches of the [USN:L6N45L10G TEXT:"league's financial rules"] over nine years and their failure to co-operate with the investigation.
City have denied wrongdoing and have appealed against the decision.
On the pitch, champions Arsenal climbed to second in the table on 15 points, behind City on goal difference before the Manchester club travel to Liverpool on Sunday.
Chelsea struck twice in the opening three minutes en route to a 5-1 thrashing of Bournemouth, with Jordan Henderson and Joao Pedro bagging two goals apiece, and are fifth on 10 points.
Tottenham Hotspur struck in stoppage time to salvage a 1-1 draw at Manchester United as both sides' struggles continued.
Brighton & Hove Albion climbed to third, two points off top spot, with a 2-0 win at Sunderland.
Aston Villa and visiting Brentford drew 2-2, while Ipswich Town edged Fulham 2-1 at Portman Road with a last-gasp goal to leave the last-placed London side without a league victory this season.
FRUSTRATING FIRST HALF Arsenal were looking to bounce back, having slumped to a 3-0 defeat at Brighton in the last game before the break but endured a frustrating first half as they struggled to create chances.
Their play improved in the second period, but Leeds took the lead in the 55th minute when James Justin slammed home a clever pull-back from Gabriel Gudmundsson.
Riccardo Calafiori levelled for Arsenal seven minutes later, the Italian jumping to steer home Ben White's knock-down and, sensing his side could grab all three points, manager Mikel Arteta rang the changes.
He sent on Guimaraes, Jurrien Timber and Viktor Gyokeres, and was rewarded when Guimaraes grabbed the winner with a brilliantly worked goal in the 70th minute, sending a low shot into the far corner of the net from the edge of the box.
"It was such a difficult game, obviously after the international break it's never easy, especially after a defeat in our last game," Calafiori said.
"I think we had some tough moments, but I think we deserved the winner. We acted well after the goal we conceded."
Leeds are sixth on nine points.
UNLIKELY HERO At Stamford Bridge, Henderson was Chelsea's unlikely hero, opening the scoring in the second minute when Cole Palmer, fresh from signing a new contract, drove forward from the halfway line before setting him up to score.
Chelsea struck again a minute later when Henderson found Morgan Rogers, whose curling effort deflected in off defender Antonio Silva.
Chelsea extended their lead 40 seconds after halftime through Joao Pedro before Evanilson pulled one back for the visitors five minutes later. Joao Pedro netted the Blues' fourth before Henderson capped the win with a superb curling free kick.
Henderson, 36, became the oldest player to be directly involved in three-plus Premier League goals since Cristiano Ronaldo in April 2022.
At Old Trafford, Spurs were the better team but United punished their wastefulness in the 73rd minute when Matheus Cunha picked out Bryan Mbeumo in the box, and Mbeumo slotted home with United's second shot on target.
Rodrigo Bentancur was shown a red card for headbutting Luke Shaw during a 78th-minute melee.
But 10-man Spurs equalised in the 92nd minute when Dominic Solanke got away from Lisandro Martinez to nod Sandro Tonali's cross home for a well-deserved leveller that got them off the bottom of the table. They are 18th on three points, while United are 12th with six points.
Brighton's Maxim de Cuyper and Jaouen Hadjam scored in the second half for their side, whose victory came despite seeing Pascal Struijk red-carded in the 57th minute.
Brentford's Kristoffer Ajer struck in the 79th to salvage a draw at Villa that left his team fourth on 10 points. Yehor Yarmolyuk had opened the scoring for the visitors before Nicolas Jackson and John McGinn replied for Villa.
Ipswich captain Dara O'Shea scored in the 92nd minute to snatch victory over Fulham, who led through Ryan Sessegnon until the 88th minute when Abdoul Ouattara fired in a fine equaliser.

Oct 10 (Reuters) – A conversation on Friday between President Vladimir Putin and US President Donald Trump was “very substantive and friendly” and neither leader wanted to be the first to end the call, Russian news agency Interfax quoted a Kremlin aide as saying.

During the call, the presidents agreed that Russia would supply diesel to the US and global markets to lower fuel prices, prompting an unexpected temporary easing of US sanctions on Russian fuel that has dismayed Ukraine.

The Kremlin said most of the conversation focused on efforts to resolve the war in Ukraine. Putin also downplayed the likelihood of three-way peace talks resuming soon. 

Show Full Article

Interfax cited Kremlin foreign policy aide Yuri Ushakov on Saturday as saying the conversation lasted an hour and a half.

“Neither wanted to be the first to hang up,” he said. “They hung up simultaneously, literally at the same time.”

Kyiv is relying on US support in negotiations to end the war. After news of the call broke on Friday, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy condemned the diesel deal in unusually blunt terms, calling it a “weak decision” and “an investment in a war that must be ended.”

The West imposed sanctions, including restrictions on Russian energy imports, after Moscow launched the full-scale war in Ukraine in February 2022. Efforts to end the fighting have so far stalled, partly over Russia’s demand for four Ukrainian regions it does not fully control. 

On Friday, negotiators from the US, Ukraine and European countries held talks in Miami aimed at reaching agreement on a unified peace proposal in the coming weeks that could be presented to Russia, according to a person familiar with the discussions.

(Reporting by Alessandra Prentice; Editing by Joe Bavier)

items.title: Spanish lawyer Gonzalez Durantez launches centrist party for November election
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Lawyer Miriam Gonzalez Durantez launched a new Spanish political party on Saturday to run in an early general election on November 29, promising to rise above a growing ideological divide, recover democratic values and depoliticise institutions.
items.body:
Lawyer Miriam Gonzalez Durantez launched a new Spanish political party on Saturday to run in an [USN:L1N45V07B TEXT:"early general election"] on November 29, promising to rise above a growing ideological divide, recover democratic values and depoliticise institutions.
Gonzalez Durantez, who is married to former British Deputy Prime Minister Nick Clegg and specialises in international and EU trade law, said the party, called Democracy21, will run in the election in Madrid and Barcelona.
The party enters a volatile political landscape after Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez called the snap election on Monday following parliament's rejection of measures to address a [USN:L8N45Q06Q TEXT:"mounting housing crisis"]. Opinion polls point to the conservative People's Party (PP) and far-right Vox likely winning a combined parliamentary majority.
Referring to the left-right political divide in Spain exemplified by the deep rivalry between the Socialists and the PP, she criticised "two rigid blocs with nothing to foster consensus".
Gonzalez Durantez called on Spaniards to "set aside our ideological differences, to stand united, and to work together to safeguard democracy and modernise the country."
The crisis has triggered continuing mass protests over home shortages and surging rents, stoked by the eviction of an 87-year-old woman, whose death on Tuesday further angered protesters.
Gonzalez Durantez blamed both the ruling coalition and the opposition, which controls most of Spain's regions, for the housing crisis, calling their politicians "a cost, a burden for the country" who expressly failed to develop and urbanise the land.
"They haven't used the permits to build housing; instead, they've used them to line the coffers of their city councils. They've imposed so many regulations, many of them absurd, that they've doubled the price per square meter of construction and have made it almost impossible for us to build affordable housing," she told supporters.
Central government can set housing legislation and devise nationwide plans for incentives and subsidies, but their implementation, and wider urban planning, is largely devolved to regional governments and municipalities.
She said she would identify a problem and not play politics with it. "I won’t use it to pit one group against another, no, I’ll simply fix it."

items.title: Home favourite Zheng sets up China Open final against Andreeva
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: French Open winner Mirra Andreeva will face Olympic champion and home favourite Zheng Qinwen in the China Open final after the Russian fourth seed eased past Nikola Bartunkova and unseeded Zheng overpowered Elise Mertens in Saturday's semi-finals.
items.body:
French Open winner Mirra Andreeva will face Olympic champion and home favourite Zheng Qinwen in the China Open final after the Russian fourth seed eased past Nikola Bartunkova and unseeded Zheng overpowered Elise Mertens in Saturday's semi-finals.
Zheng, who received a wildcard entry to the tournament after recovering from an elbow injury, became the first Chinese player to reach the final in Beijing as she outplayed Belgian 13th seed Mertens 7-5 6-2 after Andreeva crushed Bartunkova 6-2 6-2.
Zheng made an early break to build a 4-2 lead, but made a number of errors to hand Mertens the break back.
But the 24-year-old, who is chasing her first WTA 1000 title on home soil, remained calm to build a 6-5 lead, before her strong crosscourt forehand earned her another break point which she converted when Mertens netted.
Zheng dominated the second set to secure her second clash with Andreeva, having beaten the Russian when they met in the 2024 Beijing quarter-finals.
"I always want to give my best here. It's like the fifth Grand Slam for me," said Zheng, who reached the semi-final in 2024.
In the first semi-final, Andreeva took an hour and 14 minutes to beat Bartunkova and reach her second WTA 1000 final of the year.
Czech Bartunkova committed 20 unforced errors, twice as many as Andreeva, as the world number five hit 27 winners to clinch victory.
Andreeva is relishing her first China Open final.
"Of course, we all know that (Zheng) is playing at home. That's okay. Also, she's been coming back, she's been playing better, she's been beating a lot of great players," the 19-year-old told reporters.

items.title: Palmer firma un contrato con el Chelsea hasta 2034
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: El centrocampista ofensivo del Chelsea, Cole Palmer, firmó una ampliación de contrato que le mantendrá en Stamford Bridge hasta 2034, anuncio el sábado el club de la Premier League.
items.body:
El centrocampista ofensivo del Chelsea, Cole Palmer, firmó una ampliación de contrato que le mantendrá en Stamford Bridge hasta 2034, anuncio el sábado el club de la Premier League.
El internacional inglés, de 24 años, se ha convertido en una figura clave desde que llegó al Chelsea procedente del Manchester City en 2023, con un registro de 91 goles en 138 partidos en todas las competiciones.
Formó parte de la plantilla que ganó el Mundial de Clubes y la UEFA Conference League.
"Hablé con los propietarios, con los directores deportivos y, por supuesto, con el entrenador, y me transmitieron mucha confianza, así que lo lógico era firmar", dijo Palmer.
"Al hablar también con los jugadores, veo que todos comparten las mismas ambiciones. Tengo la sensación de que aquí ganaremos grandes títulos constantemente".
El Chelsea ha acordado contratos a largo plazo con varios jugadores del primer equipo y con jóvenes promesas.
El delantero João Pedro firmó recientemente un contrato hasta 2034, y el extremo Pedro Neto acordó el mes pasado un contrato de seis años.

items.title: La presidencia irlandesa de la UE quiere un recorte del 8% al proyecto de presupuesto para 2028-2034
items.author: Jan Strupczewski, Yun Chee Foo
items.creator: Jan Strupczewski, Yun Chee Foo
items.summary: La presidencia irlandesa de la Unión Europea (UE) propuso el sábado un recorte del 8% al proyecto de presupuesto de la Comisión Europea para el periodo 2028-2034, a 1,6 billones de euros (1,79 billones de dólares), lo que ha suscitado críticas por parte de los Estados miembros más austeros, que consideran que la reducción no es suficiente.
items.body:
La presidencia irlandesa de la Unión Europea (UE) propuso el sábado un recorte del 8% al proyecto de presupuesto de la Comisión Europea para el periodo 2028-2034, a 1,6 billones de euros (1,79 billones de dólares), lo que ha suscitado críticas por parte de los Estados miembros más austeros, que consideran que la reducción no es suficiente.
La propuesta irlandesa supone, a pesar de todo, un aumento del 30% respecto del presupuesto actual del bloque, que abarca el periodo de 2021 a 2027. El presupuesto de la UE es la principal fuente de financiación de todas las políticas fundamentales del bloque de 27 países.
La Comisión, el órgano ejecutivo de la UE, ha señalado que el bloque debe destinar más fondos a la defensa y al impulso de la competitividad europea, mientras que algunos Estados miembros desean mantener la mayor parte del gasto destinado al apoyo a la agricultura y al desarrollo regional.
"La 'caja de negociación' supone un ahorro del 8%, es decir, 141.000 millones de euros, respecto a la propuesta original de la Comisión", dijo Irlanda, que actualmente y por seis meses preside la UE, refiriéndose a su propuesta de compromiso.
Irlanda ajustó la cifra original de la Comisión, de 2 billones de euros, teniendo en cuenta la inflación en siete años, situándola en 1,76 billones de euros a precios de 2025, lo que supuso una reducción del 8%.
"Tal y como lo vemos, el marco de negociación sirve para salvar las numerosas diferencias entre los Estados miembros", dijo el ministro irlandés Thomas Byrne en una rueda de prensa.
"Nos acerca a la resolución del trilema presupuestario, abordando las conversaciones sobre la mejor forma de financiar nuevas prioridades en materia de competitividad, investigación, innovación, seguridad y defensa, al tiempo que se abordan las políticas fundamentales", añadió.
La propuesta establece un recorte del 3% del gasto en desarrollo regional, agricultura y pesca respecto de las propias cifras de la Comisión —la partida más importante del presupuesto— y una reducción del 13% en el gasto en competitividad y seguridad.
Los líderes de la UE debatirán la propuesta irlandesa en Bruselas el 15 y 16 de octubre. El presupuesto de la UE, conocido como Marco Financiero Plurianual, debe ser aprobado por los 27 Estados miembros.
(1 dólar = 0,8928 euros)

items.title: Abbas postpones Palestinian elections, sets presidential poll for September 2027
items.author: Ali Sawafta, Nidal Al-Mughrabi, Eman Abouhassira
items.creator: Ali Sawafta, Nidal Al-Mughrabi, Eman Abouhassira
items.summary: Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas on Saturday postponed legislative elections due next month until September 11, 2027, and called a presidential poll for the same date, blaming Israel and the security situation in the Palestinian territories for the delay.
items.body:
Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas on Saturday postponed legislative elections due next month until September 11, 2027, and called a presidential poll for the same date, blaming Israel and the security situation in the Palestinian territories for the delay.
Abbas' decree cited "obstacles posed by Israeli measures" and the need to establish suitable political, security and on-the-ground conditions for "free, fair and inclusive elections", the official Palestinian news agency WAFA reported.
In a post on X, Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar, pointing to the last Palestinian election having been held two decades ago, rejected Abbas' remarks as "yet another ridiculous lie designed to evade responsibility and accountability."
There had been serious doubts that the [USN:L8N45G1M5 TEXT:"Palestinian Authority vote"] would go ahead next month. The Palestinians have not held legislative or presidential elections since 2005-2006, after which Abbas' rival, the Islamist group Hamas, seized control of Gaza, ousting his loyalists.
Abbas has governed by decree since his presidential mandate expired in 2009.
The Palestinian Authority held municipal elections in April in the West Bank and in Deir al-Balah in central Gaza, the only city in the enclave to participate. The vote was the first election held in Gaza since 2006.
The decree said Israeli military attacks, settlement expansion, settler violence and movement restrictions in the West Bank, including East Jerusalem, along with Israel's continued withholding of Palestinian tax revenues, created challenges to preparing for and holding elections this November.
In Gaza , the decree pointed to "exceptional security and humanitarian conditions", the incomplete withdrawal of Israeli forces, the lack of progress in reconstruction and the failure to implement arrangements for deploying international stabilisation forces and police.
The decree called on Palestinians in Jerusalem, the West Bank and Gaza to vote.
Israeli restrictions on access for election commission staff and international observers to Gaza and East Jerusalem also complicated preparations, the decree said.
Israel typically bans the Palestinian Authority from holding elections in East Jerusalem, territory it captured in the 1967 war and later annexed in a move most countries do not recognize.
The decision to postpone followed consultations with Palestinian factions and political forces. It also aimed to allow time for a comprehensive Palestinian national dialogue to strengthen unity and address challenges facing the electoral process.
PLEDGE TO HOLD VOTE AFTER TWO DECADES Two Palestinian officials told Reuters on Thursday that leaders of Abbas' Fatah movement and rival Hamas had agreed at a meeting in Cairo on Wednesday to postpone the elections.
An August poll by the West Bank-based Palestinian Center for Policy and Survey Research (PSR) showed declining support for both Hamas and Fatah, which many Palestinians in Gaza and the West Bank blame for their continuing political divisions.
The delay comes just weeks after Abbas reaffirmed the November election timetable in his September 24 address to the UN General Assembly, as he sought to advance internationally backed reforms.
Abbas had committed in writing to French President Emmanuel Macron and Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman to hold presidential and legislative elections as part of France's recognition of a Palestinian state in September 2025.
France's foreign ministry [USN:L1N45V090 TEXT:"said on Thursday"] that holding the elections was essential, and it welcomed the launch of an EU election observation mission.

items.title: Report à 2027 des élections palestiniennes
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Le président palestinien Mahmoud Abbas a annulé samedi les élections législatives prévues en novembre en raison de la dégradation de la situation dans les territoires palestiniens et fixé au 11 septembre 2027 la tenue simultanée des élections présidentielle et législatives, a rapporté l'agence de presse officielle palestinienne WAFA.
items.body:
Le président palestinien Mahmoud Abbas a annulé samedi les élections législatives prévues en novembre en raison de la dégradation de la situation dans les territoires palestiniens et fixé au 11 septembre 2027 la tenue simultanée des élections présidentielle et législatives, a rapporté l'agence de presse officielle palestinienne WAFA.
Le décret de Mahmoud Abbas évoque les "obstacles créés par les mesures israéliennes" à la tenue des élections en novembre ainsi que la nécessité de réunir des conditions politiques, sécuritaires et de terrain adaptées à l'organisation d'"élections libres, équitables et inclusives".
Il appelle les Palestiniens de Jérusalem, de Cisjordanie et de Gaza à participer au scrutin.
De sérieux doutes existaient quant à la tenue du scrutin de l'Autorité palestinienne à la fin novembre. Les Palestiniens n'ont plus organisé d'élections législatives ni présidentielle depuis 2005-2006, à l'issue desquelles le Hamas, rival islamiste du président palestinien Mahmoud Abbas, a pris le contrôle de Gaza en évinçant ses partisans.
Le décret précise que les attaques militaires israéliennes, l'expansion des colonies, les violences de colons et les restrictions de circulation en Cisjordanie, y compris à Jérusalem-Est, ainsi que la poursuite du gel par Israël des recettes fiscales palestiniennes, ont créé des difficultés pour préparer et organiser les élections à la date initialement prévue.
À Gaza, le décret fait état de "conditions sécuritaires et humanitaires exceptionnelles", du retrait inachevé des forces israéliennes, de l'absence de progrès dans la reconstruction et de la non-mise en oeuvre des dispositions relatives au déploiement de forces internationales de stabilisation et de police.
Les restrictions imposées par Israël à l'accès de Gaza et de Jérusalem-Est pour les personnels de la commission électorale et les observateurs internationaux ont également compliqué les préparatifs, ajoute le décret.
La décision de report fait suite à une résolution du comité exécutif de l'Organisation de libération de la Palestine (OLP) et à des consultations avec les factions palestiniennes et les forces politiques. Elle vise également à laisser le temps nécessaire à un dialogue national palestinien global afin de renforcer l'unité et de répondre aux défis auxquels est confronté le processus électoral.

items.body:
Nine dead in Erie, Pennsylvania, mass shooting
Reuters | Updated: 11-10-2026 01:32 IST | Created: 11-10-2026 01:32 IST

SHARE

Key Takeaways
AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Nine people were confirmed dead in Erie, Pennsylvania, authorities said, after what Governor Josh Shapiro called a "tragic mass shooting."
The incident occurred late on Friday and investigators determined that all deaths occurred before officers arrived at the scene, a statement from the city of Erie said on Saturday. "I’ve spoken with Mayor Devlin and offered my Administration’s full support following the tragic mass shooting in Erie last night — killing nine of our fellow Pennsylvanians," Shapiro wrote in a Saturday morning post on X, referring to Mayor Daria Devlin.
Erie Police Chief Rick Lorah said in a statement following the shooting that the scene was one of the most difficult he has encountered during his tenure. “The loss of life is devastating, and the circumstances we are working through are deeply disturbing,” he said.
Lorah added that authorities were still working to establish a motive. The city said a news conference was scheduled for Saturday.

items.title: Eritrea asks UN to intervene in standoff with Ethiopia
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Eritrea asked the UN Security Council on Saturday to take deterrent measures against Ethiopia, according to a letter seen by Reuters, saying Addis Ababa's accusations of an invasion by Eritrean forces amounted to a "declaration of war".
items.body:
Eritrea asked the UN Security Council on Saturday to take deterrent measures against Ethiopia, according to a letter seen by Reuters, saying Addis Ababa's accusations of an invasion by Eritrean forces amounted to a "declaration of war".
The [USN:L6N45T121 TEXT:"incursion by Eritrean troops"], which [USN:L8N45Q06L TEXT:"Asmara has denied"] and Reuters could not independently verify, has raised fears of a return to [USN:L6N45M0WY TEXT:"all-out war"] along Ethiopia's northern border where the two Horn of Africa neighbours have clashed before.
Conflicts elsewhere in the region and tensions across the Red Sea have further raised the stakes.
Eritrean Foreign Minister Osman Saleh said in the letter that the incursion claims were part of an Ethiopian plan to justify a war of aggression. He urged the UN to intervene.
"Eritrea requests the UN Security Council to forcefully condemn Ethiopia's deplorable declaration of war against Eritrea ... and take the requisite deterrent measures against it in accordance with Chapter VII of the UN Charter," he wrote.
Chapter VII allows for measures ranging from sanctions to military action, though Osman did not specify what measures Eritrea was calling for.
Ethiopia itself [USN:L8N45V0CC TEXT:"wrote to Security Council members"] on Friday, stating that Eritrean troops had advanced up to 60 km (37 miles) inside the northern region of Tigray in recent days. It warned that the presence of foreign troops left Addis Ababa with no option but to defend itself.
Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed's spokesperson did not immediately respond to a request for comment on Saturday.
ETHIOPIAN TROOPS, MILITIA ALLIES MOVE INTO TIGRAYAN CITY Earlier in the day, Ethiopian government forces and their militia allies entered the Tigrayan city of Adigrat, near the border with Eritrea, three residents said, days after Eritrean troops [USN:L6N45U0QF TEXT:"were "][USN:L6N45U0QF TEXT:"pushed back"] from the strategic city.
A video shared on social media and verified by Reuters showed members of a militia allied with the Ethiopian government walking in the streets of Adigrat, which is located 30 km (19 miles) from the border with Eritrea.
Three Adigrat residents also told Reuters they had seen the Ethiopian army and an allied militia in the city on Saturday morning, with one of the residents saying they saw soldiers on patrol along with military vehicles.
Explosions were reported on Wednesday and Thursday near Adigrat, as the US-based conflict monitor ACLED said Ethiopia used drone strikes against Eritrean forces, who then withdrew from positions near the city.
The explosions continued on Friday, according to an Adigrat resident, who told Reuters they had heard repeated explosions overnight and into the morning several kilometres outside town.
ETHIOPIAN SEA ACCESS A FLASH POINT Eritrean Information Minister Yemane Gebremeskel said on Friday that Eritrea had shown restraint. He said a 2023 statement by landlocked Ethiopia that it would acquire sovereign access to the sea amounted to declaring a war of aggression against his country.
Ethiopia had access to a coastline for decades until Eritrea gained independence from Addis Ababa in 1993. Ethiopia argues that restoring sea access is an existential issue but has said it would be restored through peace and dialogue.
Ethiopia has accused Eritrea of backing the rebel alliance that has been battling government troops since September 23 in its northern regions of Tigray, Amhara and Afar. Eritrea has denied doing so.
After years of war, Eritrea and Ethiopia made peace in a 2018 agreement that earned Ethiopia's Abiy the Nobel Peace Prize. Eritrea fought in support of Ethiopia’s federal government during a 2020-2022 civil war in Tigray, but relations soured again toward the end of that conflict.
The fighting that broke out last month has been the biggest escalation of violence since the Tigray war, in which hundreds of thousands died.

items.title: Ukraine-Une attaque russe fait 20 morts à Zaporijjia, passe d'armes Zelensky-Trump
items.author: Sergiy Chalyi, Max Hunder
items.creator: Sergiy Chalyi, Max Hunder
items.summary: Vingt personnes, dont trois enfants, ont été tuées samedi lors d'une attaque russe contre la ville de Zaporijjia, dans le sud de l'Ukraine, au lendemain de l'annonce par le président américain Donald Trump d'un accord levant les sanctions sur le diesel russe, un revers majeur pour Kyiv.
items.body:
Vingt personnes, dont trois enfants, ont été tuées samedi lors d'une attaque russe contre la ville de Zaporijjia, dans le sud de l'Ukraine, au lendemain de l'annonce par le président américain Donald Trump d'un accord levant les sanctions sur le diesel russe, un revers majeur pour Kyiv.
Une fillette de six ans figure parmi les victimes d'une frappe qui a réduit une partie d'un immeuble résidentiel à l'état de gravats.
Dix-huit autres personnes ont été blessées dans cette attaque contre Zaporijjia, ville industrielle dont la périphérie se situe à moins de 30 km de la ligne de front.
"Aujourd'hui, la Russie a fêté la levée des sanctions sur les exportations de diesel en larguant cinq bombes planantes sur des immeubles résidentiels à Zaporijjia", a déclaré le président ukrainien Volodimir Zelensky, dans l'une de ses critiques les plus virulentes à ce jour à l'encontre de la Maison blanche.
Donald Trump a rétorqué que Volodimir Zelensky "ferait mieux d'arrêter immédiatement" de bombarder les raffineries russes, ajoutant : "Je suggère qu'ils (les Ukrainiens, NDLR) se trouvent un nouveau dirigeant capable de conclure un accord."
L'attaque russe de samedi est la dernière en date d'une série de frappes particulièrement meurtrières en Ukraine ces dernières semaines. Près de 80 civils ont été tués lors de frappes russes mercredi et jeudi, dont au moins 30 dans un bombardement contre la ville-garnison de Kramatorsk, dans l'est du pays, et 22 autres dans une attaque de missile contre la ville de Pryluky, située à environ 130 km à l'est de Kyiv.
Le gouverneur local, Mykhaïlo Semikine, a déclaré que la Russie avait frappé plusieurs sites simultanément dans les premières heures de samedi.
Des secouristes ont progressé à travers les décombres pour extraire vivants d'autres habitants de l'immeuble. Un homme, dont la jambe était coincée sous les gravats, criait de douleur pendant qu'il était dégagé.
"D'AUTRES SIGNAUX SONT NÉCESSAIRES" Zaporijjia, qui comptait plus de 700.000 habitants avant la guerre, est régulièrement visée par les bombardements russes, dont l'intensité s'est accrue au cours des derniers mois.
"La nuit dernière a constitué une nouvelle confirmation que la Russie considère tout allègement de la pression comme un signal lui permettant soi-disant de continuer à faire la guerre, de continuer à larguer des bombes sur les villes. D'autres signaux sont nécessaires", a déclaré Volodimir Zelensky.
Une attaque de missile menée samedi après-midi a également frappé un restaurant à Kyiv, blessant sept personnes.
Des drones russes ont survolé la capitale ukrainienne tout au long de la journée dans le cadre d'une nouvelle vague massive de bombardements, la plus importante depuis les premiers jours de la guerre.
Le ministère russe de la Défense a déclaré samedi en début se soirée que ses drones avaient frappé plus tôt un centre de traitement de données à Kyiv ainsi qu'un cargo transportant des fournitures militaires vers le port ukrainien d'Odessa.
Dans un communiqué, il a ajouté que le site de Kyiv était utilisé par les forces armées ukrainiennes pour collecter, traiter et stocker des renseignements. Reuters n'a pas été en mesure de vérifier ces informations dans l'immédiat.
La décision de Donald Trump de lever les sanctions sur les exportations de diesel russe intervient alors que son administration cherche à enrayer la hausse des prix des carburants, qui ont bondi dans le contexte du conflit opposant les États-Unis à l'Iran.
Kyiv avait au contraire exhorté Washington à accroître la pression sur la Russie afin de la contraindre à engager de véritables négociations pour mettre fin à la guerre, qui dure depuis quatre ans et demi.
L'ACCORD SUR LE DIESEL A PRIS KYIV PAR SURPRISE Donald Trump a en outre critiqué les frappes ukrainiennes contre les raffineries russes, estimant qu'elles avaient contribué à faire grimper les prix mondiaux. Kyiv dit vouloir un arrêt total des attaques visant les infrastructures énergétiques des deux camps, alors que Moscou continue de pilonner le réseau électrique ukrainien.
Samedi, plusieurs secteurs de Kyiv et de sa région ont été privés d'électricité, provoquant l'arrêt complet du métro de la capitale pour la deuxième fois de la semaine.
Ces dernières frappes sont intervenues après des discussions à Miami entre responsables ukrainiens et européens et négociateurs américains, vendredi, en vue d'élaborer une proposition commune pour mettre fin à la guerre, selon une source proche du dossier.
L'agence de presse officielle russe Tass, citant une source, a rapporté samedi que les émissaires américains Steve Witkoff et Jared Kushner pourraient se rendre à Moscou au cours des deux prochaines semaines.
Donald Trump a annoncé l'accord sur le diesel alors que les négociations de vendredi étaient en cours, une décision qui, selon Volodimir Zelensky, a pris Kyiv par surprise.
Le président russe Vladimir Poutine a déclaré, à l'issue d'un entretien téléphonique avec son homologue américain, qu'une reprise immédiate des pourparlers de paix était peu probable, invoquant les attaques de drones ukrainiens contre Moscou.
Par ailleurs, quatre civils ont été tués et cinq autres blessés à la suite d'attaques ukrainiennes contre la région de Louhansk, sous contrôle russe dans l'est de l'Ukraine, a déclaré samedi le gouverneur local installé par Moscou.
Reuters n'a pas été en mesure de vérifier cette information de manière indépendante et l'Ukraine n'a pas fait de commentaire dans l'immédiat.

items.title: Isaias kills four, about 670,000 without power after landfall
items.summary: Four people died after Hurricane Isaias made landfall early on Saturday, and about 670,000 residents in Florida, Alabama, Georgia and Mississippi were still without power as the storm weakened to a ...
items.body:
Isaias kills four, about 670,000 without power after landfall
Reuters | Updated: 11-10-2026 01:06 IST | Created: 11-10-2026 01:06 IST

SHARE

Key Takeaways
AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Four people died after Hurricane Isaias made landfall early on Saturday, and about 670,000 residents in Florida, Alabama, Georgia and Mississippi were still without power as the storm weakened to a post-tropical cyclone, according to local authorities and electricity monitoring services. Two of the deaths resulted from trees falling on homes, according to local media and authorities.
Authorities in Florida had received no search and rescue requests shortly after landfall in a sign of limited impact, Governor Ron DeSantis said. But hazardous conditions remained and storm surges, flash flooding, damaging winds and a risk of tornadoes across parts of the US Southeast were expected, the National Hurricane Center said. The tornado threat is expected to continue on Saturday across parts of the Florida Panhandle, Georgia and the Carolinas, the NHC said.
In Florida, power restoration was marked as a priority, authorities said, while highways, bridges and airports were reopening, and teams were assessing the damage. "They're going to make assessments this morning, and I think that'll give us a good sense about the future for the rapidity of the power restoration," DeSantis told a press conference in Tallahassee. Some 16,000 utility linemen had prepared to respond to the storm, he said.
About 420,000 customers in Florida, 190,000 in Alabama, 43,000 in Georgia and 17,000 in Mississippi had no power as of midday Saturday, according to tracking firm PowerOutage.us. A separate storm on the Pacific Ocean, Rachel, was moving toward the coast of northern Baja California on Saturday, bringing wind gusts and increased tides, which left another 7,000 people without power in California.
Alabama's emergency management agency said the downed trees and power lines made travel hazardous in Houston County, which is under a flash flood warning. "Due to the impacts of Hurricane Isaias, all Houston County roads are closed until further notice," it posted on X.
A category 2 hurricane when it hit Florida's coast and the first of the 2026 Atlantic season, Isaias is expected to produce gusty winds well inland before weakening below gale force later on Saturday, the NHC said. On Saturday, oil and gas producer Shell said it was beginning to redeploy personnel to its Mars, Olympus, Ursa, Vito and Appomattox assets in the Gulf, whileChevron was advancing efforts to redeploy staff to its platforms and seeking to restore full production. "Remobilization of crews will continue through Sunday," it said.
Despite the progress, about 69% of oil output and 57% of natural gas production in the US Gulf of Mexico remained shut on Saturday, slightly down from Friday numbers, the Marine Minerals Administration said. Some 113 production platforms representing 30% of the total remained evacuated, according to the agency.
President Donald Trump, asked about hurricane preparations on Friday, told reporters outside the White House that it was "under control." The US Energy Department said on Saturday it authorized an emergency exchange of up to 4 million barrels of crude oil from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve to address supply disruptions due to the hurricane. Emergency declarations were approved in Florida and Alabama to ensure federal resources would be available to respond to Isaias, Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said on X.
"There's also a lot of hazards post-storm that people should be careful of, but so far, we've had a lot of assets in place that have not been called on," DeSantis told FOX News early on Saturday. In the coastal city of Pensacola, a lack of drinking water is a problem, the mayor said. Pensacola airport, Florida's 10th largest, was damaged by the storm and is closed to commercial flights until further notice.

items.title: Norris apologises after collision dashes McLaren sprint hopes
items.author: Rohith Nair
items.creator: Rohith Nair
items.summary: World champion Lando Norris apologised to his McLaren team after a final-lap collision with team mate Oscar Piastri wrecked their pursuit of a podium finish at a chaotic Singapore Grand Prix sprint on Saturday.
items.body:
World champion Lando Norris apologised to his McLaren team after a final-lap collision with team mate Oscar Piastri wrecked their pursuit of a podium finish at a [USN:L1N45W02M TEXT:"chaotic Singapore Grand Prix sprint"] on Saturday.
The McLaren duo were chasing Ferrari's Charles Leclerc, who was struggling with his tyres in the dying stages of the 20-lap sprint, when disaster struck on the final lap.
Norris, running fifth behind Piastri in fourth, attempted to overtake his team mate but clipped the Australian's rear tyre with his front wheel, sending both cars spinning and handing Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli fourth place.
"Sorry about that. Obviously I didn't want that to happen but I thought I was fully alongside. I just ran out of space at the apex but I was there," Norris said over the team radio.
While Norris limped home to eighth place to claim the final point available, Piastri was forced to retire as he became one of nine cars that did not finish - a record number of retirements for a Formula One sprint race.
"I'd rather just go back and review it," Norris told Sky Sports.
"I apologised to them that one of the cars is out but, like I said, the rest of it we'll go review."
Piastri said he had not seen the incident properly to comment but downplayed its significance as they were not in high points scoring positions.
"From where I sit, it's for fourth and fifth for a sprint race, so I'm not that bothered either way," Piastri said.
"Just obviously it's a lot of work now for the team to get both cars fixed (ahead of qualifying for Sunday's race). Just a shame for the team."
'SIMPLY NOT ACCEPTABLE' Both McLaren drivers were summoned to meet the stewards after the collision but no further action was taken.
The FIA said both drivers "contributed to the incident and that neither driver was wholly or predominantly to blame for the collision."
McLaren team principal Andrea Stella was not impressed with his drivers, however, adding that scoring just one point was not enough.
"Seeing two McLarens making contact like that is simply not acceptable. This is something that we will discuss with our drivers," he said.
"We will do it in private. We will reiterate that the team interest is far bigger than any of us. There's no ego, there's no person that is bigger than the interest of the McLaren Formula One team.
"I'm sure, like always, this will be conversations that will lead to the team being more united and even stronger."
Red Bull's Max Verstappen won the sprint and the Dutchman, who also [USN:L1N45W02M TEXT:"clinched pole for Sunday's race"] , leapfrogged Norris to climb to fifth in the world championship standings.

items.title: EU's Irish presidency wants 8% cut to proposed 2028-2034 budget plan
items.author: Jan Strupczewski, Yun Chee Foo
items.creator: Jan Strupczewski, Yun Chee Foo
items.summary: The Irish EU presidency proposed on Saturday an 8% cut in the European Commission's budget plan for the period 2028 to 2034 to €1.6 trillion ($1.79 trillion), drawing criticism from more frugal member states that the reduction is not deep enough.
items.body:
The Irish EU presidency proposed on Saturday an 8% cut in the European Commission's budget plan for the period 2028 to 2034 to €1.6 trillion ($1.79 trillion), drawing criticism from more frugal member states that the reduction is not deep enough.
The Irish proposal still marks a 30% increase over the bloc's current budget, which runs from 2021 to 2027. The EU budget is the main source of financing for all of the 27-country bloc's main policies.
The Commission, the EU executive, has said the bloc needs to spend more on defence and boosting European competitiveness, while some member states want to retain most of the expenditure to support farming and regional development.
"The Negotiating Box provides savings of 8%, or €141 billion, on the Commission's original proposal," said Ireland, current holder of the EU's six-month rotating presidency, referring to its compromise proposal.
Ireland put the Commission's original €2 trillion figure adjusted for inflation over the seven-year period at €1.76 trillion based on 2025 prices, which resulted in an 8% reduction.
IRELAND SAYS PLAN SEEKS TO RECONCILE COMPETING DEMANDS "As we see it, the negotiating box acts to bridge the many differences between the member states," Irish minister Thomas Byrne told a press conference.
"It brings us closer to resolving the budgetary trilemma, addressing the talks of how best to finance new priorities in competitiveness, research, innovation, security and defence while at the same time addressing core policies," he said.
The proposal sets out a 3% cut in spending on regional development, agriculture and fisheries from the Commission's own figures — the biggest outlay in the budget — and a 13% reduction in spending on competitiveness and security.
It foresees €55 billion in new financing options derived from customs duties, a share of the cash EU governments get from selling CO2 emissions permits to companies and an annual lump-sum contribution from large companies operating in the EU, among other sources.
Germany's Chancellor Friedrich Merz joined ministers from Sweden and the Netherlands - all three countries are net contributors to the budget - in criticising the Irish proposal.
"The EU budget must be affordable for those who bear the main burden of financing it," he said.
However, lawmakers in the European Parliament, which wants a 10% increase in the Commission's €2 trillion proposal, said the Irish plan would weaken Europe and would not win their consent.
EU leaders will discuss the Irish proposal in Brussels on October 15 to 16. The EU budget, which is known as the [USN:L8N41B114 TEXT:"Multiannual Financial Framework"], needs to be agreed by all 27 member states.
($1 = 0.8928 euros)

items.title: Israeli strikes kill five people in Gaza, medics say
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Israeli strikes killed at least five Palestinians in the Gaza Strip in two separate attacks on Saturday, health officials said.
items.body:
Israeli strikes killed at least five Palestinians in the Gaza Strip in two separate attacks on Saturday, health officials said.
Medics said an Israeli strike killed four people near Panda Mall in Gaza City, while another killed one person in the Tuffah neighbourhood further south of the city.
The Israeli military said the two strikes targeted militants, without giving further information.
Israel has stepped up strikes against Hamas in recent weeks, saying the Palestinian militant group has been rearming and carrying out attacks in violation of the ceasefire.
Hamas denies rebuilding its arsenal or planning attacks and accuses Israel of undermining a US-brokered ceasefire agreed a year ago.
The ceasefire calls for eventual reconstruction of the territory. But little progress has been made towards implementing a deal to end the conflict that includes terms for Hamas to disarm and Israel to withdraw its troops.
Gaza health officials have said at least 1,400 Palestinians have been killed by Israeli fire since the truce was agreed last October. Israel says four of its soldiers have been killed by militants in Gaza over the same period.
The Gaza war was triggered by the Hamas-led [USN:L1N45T04T TEXT:"October 7, 2023 attacks"] on Israel, which killed 1,200 people, while a further 251 were taken hostage.
Israel's subsequent bombardment and ground operations in Gaza have killed more than 74,000 people, according to Gaza health officials.

items.title: Palmer signs Chelsea contract until 2034
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: The England international has become a key figure since joining Chelsea from Manchester City.
items.body:
Chelsea attacking midfielder Cole Palmer has signed a contract extension to keep him at Stamford Bridge until 2034, the Premier League club said on Saturday.
The 24-year-old England international has become a key figure since joining Chelsea from Manchester City in 2023, scoring 91 goals in 138 appearances across all competitions.
He was part of the squad that won the Club World Cup and UEFA Conference League.
"Speaking to the owners, to the sporting directors and obviously the manager, they gave me a lot of confidence so it was only right to sign," Palmer said.
"Speaking to players as well, everyone has the same ambitions. I feel like we win major trophies here consistently."
Chelsea have agreed long-term contracts Chelsea with several first-team players and emerging talent.
Forward [USN:L6N44J020 TEXT:"Joao Pedro"] recently signed a deal through 2034, and winger Pedro Neto agreed a six-year contract last month.
Chelsea, 10th in the Premier League table, host Bournemouth on Saturday.

items.title: Verstappen claims first Singapore win as nine retirements mar chaotic sprint
items.author: Rohith Nair
items.creator: Rohith Nair
items.summary: The victory was the first of any kind for the Dutchman in Singapore as he took the chequered flag ahead of Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc.
items.body:
Red Bull's Max Verstappen tasted victory in Singapore for the first time as the polesitter won a chaotic sprint on Saturday after the [USN:L1N45W02H TEXT:"start was delayed by over 30 minutes"] due to heavy rain while nine cars retired, a record for sprint races.
The victory was the first of any kind for the Dutchman in Singapore as he took the chequered flag ahead of Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc.
"I want to win tomorrow. I don't see this as a win in terms of actually winning a Grand Prix," Verstappen said.
Mercedes' championship leader Kimi Antonelli was gifted fourth place after the two McLarens collided on the final lap while his team mate George Russell crashed out of the lead on lap one.
Verstappen had kept his [USN:L1N45V0HG TEXT:"pole position"] after escaping a penalty for overtaking under a yellow flag on Friday but the Dutchman made a slow start as Russell stormed ahead and Hamilton swiftly moved up from sixth to third.
Russell's sprint ended on the last turn of lap one when his rear tyre went over the kerb and he spun into the wall to bring the safety car out.
"The start was horrendous again, so that's definitely something that we need to improve on because if you have something like that tomorrow, that's your race over if nothing crazy happens," Verstappen added.
"After that, you just want to keep it calm and under control because you know that you can't pass around here."
'SILLY MISTAKE' FOR RUSSELL Russell said a miscalculation caused him to spin out at the last corner.
"I came through the corner, had more battery deployment than I thought. Pushed me a little bit wider than I hoped and then I just went on the white line," Russell said.
"Yeah, silly mistake. Big, big consequences."
The carnage continued when Lance Stroll and Sergio Perez retired after they collided and Red Bull's Isack Hadjar was asked to stop his car due to a technical issue.
The safety car remained on track after Franco Colapinto's Alpine also came to a standstill and they did not resume racing until lap seven.
Verstappen led from the Ferraris of Hamilton and Leclerc while the McLarens of Oscar Piastri and Lando Norris were in the top five ahead of Antonelli.
MCLARENS COLLIDE ON FINAL LAP McLaren's hopes of a podium vanished, however, when reigning champion Norris nudged into Piastri and the two cars spun out, allowing Antonelli to move up to fourth place and stretch his championship lead over Russell to 89 points.
"I checked in my mirrors and I saw red lights of the back of the cars of the McLarens. So I knew that something happened," Leclerc said.
The qualifying session for Sunday's race was delayed due to the rain.

items.title: Jocelyn Bioh on why Broadway is finally ready for ‘School Girls’
items.author: Kathryn Lurie
items.creator: Kathryn Lurie
items.summary: The playwright discusses what has changed since 'School Girls' was first produced, the universality of teenage insecurity and why bringing the play to Broadway feels like coming full circle.
items.body:
Nearly a decade after Jocelyn Bioh wrote “School Girls; Or, The African Mean Girls Play,” the play itself has barely changed. But the world around it has.
The comedy about a group of teenage girls at a Ghanaian boarding school premiered off-Broadway in 2017, launching Bioh’s career as a playwright and going on to become a hit at regional theaters across the United States. But despite its success, Bioh was told it might not belong on Broadway.
Now “School Girls” has made it there — following the Broadway success of Bioh’s “Jaja’s African Hair Braiding” in 2023 — and she is finding an audience that responds differently to the play’s exploration of body image, the privileging of lighter skin, known as colorism, and the often brutal social dynamics of girlhood. Beneath its rapid-fire jokes and teenage rivalries is a more painful story about who gets to be considered beautiful — and what people are willing to do to fit that ideal.
Speaking in New York City, Bioh discusses what has changed since “School Girls” was first produced, the universality of teenage insecurity and why bringing the play to Broadway feels like coming full circle.
This conversation has been edited and condensed for clarity.
How does it feel to finally bring “School Girls” to Broadway?
It feels incredibly humbling. This play changed my life. It was the first play of mine that ever got produced. I can very clearly mark what my life was like before opening night of that show and then after.
That audiences and critics all still feel the same way nearly a decade later is a reminder that I was on the right track.
It also feels doubly exciting because even though it had so much success regionally and has been all over the country, I was told, “It's a great play, but maybe it's not the right fit for a Broadway stage.”
What do you think was meant by that, and what has changed enough for it to be on Broadway now?
Broadway shows were very specific then. They didn't have ensembles that looked like the cast of “School Girls.” It was a lot of celebrities, a lot of things that seemed to fit into one specific category or box.
The world has shifted. Audiences are different than they were 10 years ago. In a lot of ways, “Jaja's African Hair Braiding” having so much success was a marker that, a Broadway play is just a play that's on Broadway. It doesn't necessarily have to fit a specific category.
Is there anything in the play that hits differently than it did when you first wrote it?
The conversation around beauty standards and body image has shifted in the last 10 years. Some would say (for the) better, some would say worse, but we're all aware of it in a different way.
The play kicks off with Paulina bullying Nana about her size and her eating. You can feel the audience is immediately on Nana's side. Halfway through the play, she has a moment where she really stands up to Paulina, and every night that moment gets applause. You can feel the audience cheering, almost jumping up ready to fight with her. They're taking off their earrings!
We did not have that experience off-Broadway. I think we were in a time where we accepted the idea that if you were somebody who was bigger, you should be losing weight; you should be trying to conform. Our ideas of beauty are very different now. Big ships turn slow, but I appreciate that I can feel that in the audience.
Did you rewrite much for this production?
Very small things, little jokes that I thought would land better. But the play is still largely the same thing I wrote in 2016.
If I were sitting down to write this play now, I don't know that I would be as honest or as vulnerable as I was then, particularly in the moments where Paulina is speaking very directly about how colorism has affected her life. I think I would censor myself a little bit now. I never thought the play would get produced, so I was very free and vulnerable in a way.
Why?
When you're a playwright and your name starts to grow within the community, you start to have an awareness of the responsibility of your words. And I'm okay with having that responsibility because I know I'm doing something really different. I'm really blowing open how people see Black and African people on a theatrical stage. There's an incredible responsibility to that.
The play takes place in Ghana, but these girls feel instantly recognizable. Did you know when you were writing it how universal they would be?
I understood that there's a real rich universality we have, particularly in school and friendship dynamics. Those things are evergreen and universal.
I knew what I was writing was different, (that) the girls and the people I was reflecting were different, but I didn't want to alienate audiences. That's part of why I added the subtitle. What's something we all know and recognize about the teenage experience? Mean girls.
Paulina seems to believe that if she can just become Miss Ghana, she can escape the limits of her life. Is her obsession with beauty really an obsession with power and possibility?
Probably. Ultimately, I think she really believes this is going to set her up for a successful life in entertainment.
The play is set in 1986, and if you became Miss Ghana, Miss World, Miss Universe — any of those things — you could become a star. This is how we have Vanessa Williams or Halle Berry or Kenya Moore, if you're of the “Real Housewives” persuasion.
(Another character,) Eloise, is a former Miss Ghana and did leave. She's come back now living a different life, (signifying that) in order to have success, you've got to get out. In order to have power, you have to get out. Maybe Paulina doesn't see the beauty and power that she can build in her own country.
That's reflective of so many immigrant, particularly African immigrant, stories: In order to have success, you need to leave. I don't know if the play were set in 2026, (if) that would be the case now. I think the play would be very different. But for Paulina and her circumstances then, that is what she believed.
The play deals so directly with colorism. Do you think colorism is in some ways more sensitive to talk about than racism?
They're inextricably linked. The play largely talks about and shows the effects of colorism, but then ends with a global lesson on racism.
And we've not moved on from it. When we started rehearsals for the play in August, the biggest news story was Lupita Nyong'o playing Helen of Troy in Christopher Nolan's film (“The Odyssey”). (Her casting) did not fit with whomever's standard of beauty (for) the woman whose face launched a thousand ships. Why didn't it fit? Why were there so many suggestions about, “Well, Zendaya's in the movie, why can't she play that part?” That's a very clear conversation about colorism, whether people are using that word or not.
When I wrote this play, it was really important for me to have that conversation because it had affected my life so much. Revisiting it now, especially in relation to these conversations that are happening globally, I'm like, well, we've not moved on from it. We can't move on from colorism because nobody's moved on from racism.
I can't change people's minds. But if people come to see “School Girls” and their implicit bias can shift just a little bit, then I've done my job.
The play is extremely funny until you realize how much pain is sitting underneath the humor. How deliberate is that?
I really believe that comedy is just a funny way of being serious. Humor and pain are on two different sides of a truth coin. It's all rooted in truth.
Paulina is a girl in the world who's trying to be affirmed and validated that she belongs there, that her beauty is widely accepted even if she knows that it's not. The lengths she goes to get there are what's comical, but it's rooted in something real that we all experience.
At the end of the day, I'm a comedic writer and I want people to be entertained. But because I know the responsibility of who I'm introducing and the culture I'm introducing, I think there's a responsibility in also educating people. If I can make that medicine go down with a little bit of sugar, honey, agave, whatever you like, I'm willing to go there.
The perspectives expressed in Culture Current are the subject’s own and do not necessarily reflect the views of Reuters News.

items.title: Amelia Earhart expedition heads to Pacific atoll hoping to find her plane
items.author: Steve Gorman
items.creator: Steve Gorman
items.summary: A US-based team of marine archaeologists has set sail for a tiny island in the far western Pacific seeking to examine the latest tantalizing clue to one of the 20th century's great unsolved mysteries: the 1937 disappearance of famed aviator Amelia Earhart.
items.body:
A US-based team of marine archaeologists has set sail for a tiny island in the far western Pacific seeking to examine the latest tantalizing clue to one of the 20th century's great unsolved mysteries: the 1937 disappearance of famed aviator Amelia Earhart.
Backed by Purdue University, an institution long affiliated with Earhart and her legacy, the group aims to learn whether a submerged object detected by satellite imagery in the island's lagoon six years ago is the wreckage of Earhart's twin-engine Lockheed Electra 10-E airplane.
Such a finding would conclusively prove the hypothesis of some scholars that Earhart and her navigator, Fred Noonan, crash-landed on or near the coral-ringed atoll and perished as castaways there, hundreds of miles from their intended refueling stop.
After embarking from Los Angeles earlier this month, the group was expected to arrive on Tuesday, October 13, local time at Nikumaroro, an uninhabited speck of land in the remote Phoenix Islands, part of the archipelago nation of the Kiribati Republic.
"Finding Amelia Earhart's Electra aircraft would be the discovery of a lifetime," Richard Pettigrew, head of the Archaeological Legacy Institute in Eugene, Oregon, who is leading the effort in conjunction with Purdue, said in press materials for the mission.
Purdue general counsel and expedition member Steve Schultz, who was in Fiji conducting advance work for the expedition last week, said in an interview: "This would be solving one of the great mysteries in aviation history, certainly one of the great mysteries of the 20th century,"
The mission has its skeptics. Chief among them is rival Earhart explorer Ric Gillespie, co-founder of TIGHAR, short for The International Group for Historic Aircraft Recovery, and author of the 2024 "One More Good Flight: The Amelia Earhart Tragedy."
TREE OR PLANE? Gillespie has led a dozen expeditions of his own to the atoll over three decades and is the leading proponent of the Nikumaroro castaway theory. But he predicted the Pettigrew-Purdue team would find no airplane wreckage or anything else of consequence left on the island.
The Purdue team credits Gillespie for laying the foundation of the theory they hope to prove. And they cite a compelling body of evidence that he has amassed over the years, including human artifacts recovered on the island, such as a 1930s-era glass cosmetic jar for freckle cream and remnants of a jackknife like one Earhart carried on the plane.
Gillespie's investigation also encompassed modern forensic analysis from records of measurements of skeletal remains found on the island in the 1940s; logs of radio transmission bearings from distress calls picked up by wireless operators in the days immediately after Earhart vanished; and a photograph taken of the island's shoreline months later showing an object that Gillespie said appears to be the Electra's landing gear.
In a Reuters interview last week, Gillespie said he believes the plane has since been lost to history, eventually swept by tides off the coral flat where it had landed largely intact and carried into the sea to sink and break apart in the surf.
Two previous attempts to locate the plane's wreckage in the surrounding ocean, including a 2019 operation conducted by marine archaeologist Robert Ballard, famed for his discovery of the wreck of the Titanic, proved fruitless, Gillespie said.
A plane-shaped sonar image from elsewhere on the sea floor turned out to be a pile of rocks.
"I'd love to find that airplane. It ain't gonna happen," Gillespie said.
Pettigrew and his team are betting otherwise. To them, the multi-branched shape first noticed in a 2020 satellite image resembles an aircraft fuselage and wings. They assert that the object, or part of it, has since been spotted in earlier aerial images of the island's lagoon dating as far back as 1938.
Gillespie said he is certain that the object in question was actually a fallen pandanus tree, a palm-like evergreen native to the island region, that washed into the lagoon.
"You can see the root ball. You can see the branches," Gillespie said in the interview. "It's a tree. People see what they want to see."
'GAS IS RUNNING LOW' The official US government view has long been that the Electra ran out of fuel and crashed at sea near its refueling destination of Howland Island, another dot of land about 400 miles northwest of Nikumaroro, then known as Gardner Island.
Earhart was last seen taking off in her Electra on July 2, 1937, from Papua New Guinea en route to Gardner, about 2,500 miles (4,000 km) to the east, during a multi-stage attempt to become the first woman to pilot a plane around the world.
Definitive radio contact with the plane was lost the next day after Earhart, 39, reported "gas is running low," followed by her final known transmission giving her geographical line of position.
The disappearance spawned the largest US government search ever undertaken for a lost aircraft, including a flyover of Gardner, but no trace of the Electra or its crew was found at the time.
The $900,000 Purdue mission, consisting of 17 people, plans to remain on Nikumaroro for five days before making the six-day return boat trip to the Kiribati capital, Tarawa, according to Schultz.
Purdue, based in West Lafayette, Indiana, would ultimately seek to bring back any bits of the Lockheed Electra that might be recovered.
Earhart was essentially a visiting faculty member at Purdue for two years as a women's career counselor and advisor to the school's aeronautics department. A Purdue research grant paid for development of the Electra, which she called her "flying laboratory."
Purdue lawyer Schultz said if the plane were found, no artifacts would be removed from it on this trip. Any effort to extract the aircraft wreckage would require further permission from the Kiribati government, he said.

items.title: 「台湾は中国の一部」、中国が台湾総統の演説非難
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［北京　１０日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［北京　１０日　ロイター］ - 中国国務院台湾事務弁公室は１０日、台湾の頼清徳総統が同日行った双十節（建国記念日）の演説について、「事実を無視し、真実をゆがめ、民衆を惑わし、下心をあらわにしている」と非難した。

同弁公室は、頼氏が演説で「『台湾独立』の分裂主義思想にかたくなに固執」し、「中国本土の脅威」を誇張したと指摘した。その上で「世界に中国は一つしかなく、台湾は中国の一部だ。これこそが台湾海峡の真の現状だ」と主張した。

台湾の将来についても「台湾同胞を含む全ての中国人民が共同で決定することができ、またそうでなければならない」と述べた。

頼清徳総統は演説で、台湾は平和を大切にするが自由を放棄することはないと述べ、台湾の人々が生存する権利は尊重されなければならないと訴えた。
